name: e1-fixed
description: ENGINE DEFECT E1 (pokemon/docs/52 sec.1; recorded in pokemon/docs/58), asserted from OUTSIDE the emulator on the FIXED side. src/level_caps.c lines 57 and 74 compare levelDifference with `>` where they need `>=`, so levelDifference == 5 indexes a [5] array at [5]. The fork under test runs GetSoftLevelCapExpValue once per boot for levelDifference 0..6 in both directions (cap-relative, so the recorded numbers do not depend on what the cap is) and leaves the results in gE1ProbeDown / gE1ProbeUp. This spec asserts the values the CORRECT clamp produces, so it PASSes on pokemon/hacks/e1fix and MUST FAIL on pokemon/hacks/e1bug. It is the mirror image of e1-buggy.json: same probes, same controls, only the two discriminating expected values differ. Running both specs against both builds gives a 2x2 matrix whose diagonal is PASS and whose off-diagonal is FAIL. One direction alone would be a weaker claim -- a spec that fails on the other build might merely be a spec that fails.
symbols_from_why: This spec probes gE1Probe* -- globals that exist ONLY in a hack fork, never in the pinned engine. pokemon/tests/test_verify_hack.py's ShippedSpecsAreWellFormed lint resolves every shipped spec's symbols against a .sym, and the engine's cannot resolve these; this key names the fork whose pokemon/hacks/<name>/pokeemerald.sym it must use instead. Forks are gitignored, so on a tree where this one has not been built the lint SKIPS the symbol half loudly rather than passing quietly. verify_hack.py itself ignores this key -- the .sym it uses comes from --rom/--sym and rom_pair.py, never from a spec.

probes.why: gE1ProbeValid. The probe sets this to 1 only after running all 14 calls with a level cap inside [8, MAX_LEVEL]. If the cap were nonsense the recorded numbers would mean nothing, so this must be 1 before any of them can be believed.

gE1ProbeCap -- GetCurrentLevelCap() as the probe saw it. NOT a discriminator and deliberately only range-asserted: with B_LEVEL_CAP_TYPE = LEVEL_CAP_FLAG_LIST the cap comes from the badge flags, and at AgbMain time the saveblock pointers are not installed yet (SetSaveBlocksPointers is called from src/intro.c). Recorded so the run is interpretable, not so it can be leaned on.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, src/level_caps.c line 74. gE1ProbeDown[5] = GetSoftLevelCapExpValue(cap+5, 6400) under B_EXP_CAP_TYPE = EXP_CAP_SOFT. levelDifference == 5 == ARRAY_COUNT(sExpScalingDown), so `>` is false and the else branch reads sExpScalingDown[5] -- one past the end.
THE DISCRIMINATOR, src/level_caps.c line 57. gE1ProbeUp[5] = GetSoftLevelCapExpValue(cap-5, 6400) under B_LEVEL_CAP_EXP_UP = TRUE. Same off-by-one on sExpScalingUp.

The whole descending row as raw bytes, gE1ProbeDown[0..6]. An exact byte-string compare -- the check class doc 55 sec.9.4 found actually discriminates. Asserting the row as well as the element means a mis-offset read cannot quietly agree.
The whole ascending row as raw bytes, gE1ProbeUp[0..6].

CONTROL. gE1ProbeDown[4] -- levelDifference 4, the last IN-BOUNDS index, identical in both builds. Its PASSing on the other build is what shows the failure is aimed at the one out-of-bounds index rather than at 'this is a different binary'.
CONTROL, the far side of the boundary. gE1ProbeDown[6] -- levelDifference 6 takes the clamped path both builds agree on.
CONTROL. gE1ProbeUp[4], last in-bounds index, identical in both builds.
CONTROL, far side. gE1ProbeUp[6], the clamped path, identical in both builds.
gMain.vblankCounter1 (include/main.h offset 0x20). The probe values came out of a machine that was executing, not out of a file on disk.
gMain.callback2 (offset 0x04), resolved against the .sym of the ROM actually under test.

assert.why: DISCRIMINATOR 1 (line 74). Expected 100. 6400 / sExpScalingDown[4] = 6400/64. The unfixed build reads index 5, which lands on __compound_literal.0 (a text string) whose first word is 3200826306, so 6400/3200826306 = 0 and this FAILS.

DISCRIMINATOR 2 (line 57). Expected 12800. 6400 + 6400/sExpScalingUp[4] = 6400 + 6400/1. The unfixed build reads index 5, which lands on sExpScalingUp's immediate neighbour sExpScalingDown[0] = 4, giving 8000, so this FAILS there.
DISCRIMINATOR 1, as the whole 7-element row, little-endian: 1600 800 400 200 100 100 100. The other build reads 1600 800 400 200 100 0 100.
DISCRIMINATOR 2, as the whole 7-element row, little-endian: 1600 7200 8000 9600 12800 12800 12800. The other build reads 1600 7200 8000 9600 12800 8000 12800.
The probe completed with a sane level cap. Without this, every number above could be an artefact of a garbage cap rather than of the arithmetic under test.
SUPPORTING ONLY. in_range is on doc 55 sec.9.4's weak list (it survives an address shift) and is never load-bearing here.
CONTROL. Must PASS on BOTH builds -- the last in-bounds index is untouched by the fix.
CONTROL, far side of the boundary. Must PASS on BOTH builds.
CONTROL. Must PASS on BOTH builds.
CONTROL, far side. Must PASS on BOTH builds.
Every sample of the row was readable.
SUPPORTING. The value was re-read many times across the run, not once at a lucky moment. sample_count is on doc 57's weak list.
The engine was alive and advancing for the whole run.
Every non-null callback resolves in THIS build's own .sym. For a build in which essentially every ROM symbol moved, that is a real statement about the --rom/--sym pairing, not a formality.
Doc 54 sec.3's boot progression, by name. It holds on BOTH builds, so a FAIL of this spec on the other build cannot be explained away as 'that build does not boot'.
